headline: Digital growth offsets Vegas softness amid pending buyout
summary_short: Caesars' Q2 FY2026 revenue rose to $2,993M (+4.3% q/q, +3.0% y/y) on Caesars Digital's iGaming/sports-betting growth and the Windsor consolidation, while net loss narrowed to $62M (diluted EPS -$0.30) from $82M a year ago as Las Vegas softened and shareholders await a vote on the proposed Fertitta Gaming buyout.
summary_long: Revenue grew 4.3% q/q and 3.0% y/y to $2,993M, led by Caesars Digital's iGaming handle and improved sports-betting hold, the March 2026 consolidation of Caesars Windsor, a Vegas-area national tournament boosting northern Nevada visitation, and Lake Tahoe/New Orleans capital projects. Las Vegas segment revenue, net income and EBITDA declined on lower leisure visitation, hotel occupancy and table-games hold. Casino and G&A expenses rose with Windsor's consolidation and expired property-tax credits; D&A fell on lower trailing capex; interest expense fell on debt paydown. Net loss narrowed to $62M (diluted EPS -$0.30) from $82M a year ago. Cash rose to $965M; long-term debt fell to $11,807M. No new guidance was issued; buybacks are paused pending the proposed Fertitta Gaming merger.

drivers.explanation: Revenue grew again as Digital's iGaming/sports-betting gains, the Windsor consolidation, and capital-project ramp-ups outweighed Las Vegas softness; net loss narrowed on lower interest expense and a tax benefit, while the pending Fertitta Gaming merger froze buybacks.

Higher casino revenue was driven by Caesars Digital's iGaming handle growth and improved sports-betting hold, the March 2026 Windsor consolidation, a northern-Nevada tournament, and Tahoe/New Orleans capital returns, partly offset by lower Las Vegas visitation and table-games hold.

Las Vegas's decline (lower leisure visitation, hotel rates, and table-games hold) and Caesars Digital's higher state gaming-tax rates outweighed Regional-segment gains from the Windsor consolidation and recent capital investments, on a year-over-year basis.

Net loss narrowed as lower interest expense (from debt paydown and lower variable rates) and a swing to a tax benefit offset higher Windsor-related operating costs and increased merger-related transaction costs.
Long-term debt declined as the company continued reducing outstanding debt, which the filing also cites as the reason interest expense fell for the quarter.
